- The dominant neurologic picture is early-onset floppy hypotonia with diminished reflexes → favors a primary neuromuscular (lower motor neuron, peripheral nerve or muscle) process over a pure central (cerebral) cause. Peripheral processes commonly cause global hypotonia + hyporeflexia.
- Early joint stiffness / clawing can reflect congenital contractures (arthrogryposis), early denervation with subsequent contracture, or primary muscle disease with contractures. Onset not recalled so could be congenital or evolving.
- Transient early nystagmus could reflect early ocular motor immaturity, ocular motor involvement in a neuromuscular or central process, or be unrelated; its resolution argues against a relentlessly progressive neurodegenerative process at this stage.
